content.title: About
content.content: Bean cake is a baked product made from ground legumes (usually beans or peas), whole‑grain flour, eggs, vegetable oil and a modest amount of sugar. The cake has a dense yet tender crumb, a subtle nutty flavor and a faint aroma of the beans.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Bean cake is popular in Asian and South American cuisines as a source of plant protein.
Baking legumes into a batter increases the bioavailability of their nutrients.
Legume‑based cake is more filling than traditional wheat‑flour cakes.
It is often used in vegetarian and vegan diets as a meat‑free snack.
When stored properly, the cake stays fresh for up to a week.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Legumes provide all essential amino acids, making the cake a good protein source for vegetarians.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion and promotes long‑lasting satiety.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Bean cake raises blood sugar slowly, which is beneficial for people with pre‑diabetes.

items.title: Contains iron and magnesium
items.content: These minerals aid energy metabolism and muscle function.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Phytochemicals in legumes help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans, peas or soy.

items.title: Phytic acid
items.content: Legumes contain phytic acid, which can reduce mineral absorption when consumed in excess.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Large portions may cause gas and bloating in sensitive people.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If the cake is prepared with added salt, intake should be monitored, especially for hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Bean cake can be enjoyed as a snack on its own, sliced and served with vegetable dips, added to salads, or used in sandwiches. It also reheats well in a microwave or toaster.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the cake in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, refrigerate (up to 7 days) or freeze (up to 3 months). Discard if any mold or off‑smell appears.
